name: CyberSource Secure Acceptance
_comment_enabled: ARMED 2026-09-28. Selectors verified against the real gateway DOM but NEVER EXERCISED — no run has reached this page. The first live run is the first test of every selector here.
_comment_status: SELECTORS VERIFIED against the real gateway DOM, supplied by the operator 2026-09-28 from the popup window that opens after 'Pay Online'. This file previously held HYPOTHESES written from a prose description, and four of them were wrong — see _comment_corrections. Everything below is now read off the actual page.
_comment_corrections: WHAT THE CAPTURE CAUGHT, all four of which would have failed on a live payment: (1) card_type is a RADIO GROUP, not a select — the hypothesised select[name=card_type] matched nothing; (2) the card type is a processor CODE, 001/002, not the word 'visa'; (3) the submit control is name='commit' value='Pay', not name='submit'; (4) City, Postcode and Address Line 2 are all aria-required='true' on this gateway, and the client record supplies none of them. This is exactly why selectors are captured rather than guessed.
_comment_encryption: The gateway RSA-encrypts the card fields IN THE BROWSER before submitting. Confirmed in the capture: an <input type='hidden' id='jwk'> carries the RSA public key, each card input has a disabled sibling <input class='encrypted' name='__e.card_number'>, and a script#payEncInit intercepts form.onsubmit to run RsaOaep.prepareFormForSubmission before letting it through. So the bot types into the VISIBLE inputs and lets the page's own JavaScript encrypt, exactly as it does for a human. Never write to the __e.* inputs: that means reimplementing their crypto against an undocumented contract they can change without notice.
_comment_accepted: ONLY these two. The captured radio group offers Visa (001) and Mastercard (002) and nothing else — no amex, despite card.py supporting it. Checked BEFORE anything is typed: a card the gateway does not take cannot be made to work by trying, and finding out mid-payment leaves a booking stranded on an unpaid page.
_comment_card_type_codes: The processor's own codes. The word 'visa' selects nothing — the radio's value is '001'. This mapping belongs to the processor, so it lives here rather than in card.py or gateway.py.

card_fields._comment_type: A RADIO GROUP, not a select. {value} is substituted with the processor code from card_type_codes above.
card_fields._comment_expiry: Two selects. Month options are zero-padded ('01'..'12') and year options are four-digit ('2026'..'2047'), which is what card.py already produces — expiry_month is .zfill(2) and expiry_year is widened to four digits on load.
card_fields._comment_name: Empty, and CORRECT for this gateway: the captured page has no cardholder-name field. The name is taken from the billing forename/surname.
card_fields._comment_cvn: maxlength=4. The field accepts both 3- and 4-digit CVNs even though this gateway takes no amex.

billing_fields.name: address_line_2
billing_fields._comment: Marked aria-required on the gateway, which is unusual for a second address line but is what the page says. The client record does supply this one.

billing_fields.name: city
billing_fields._comment: *** NOT ON THE CLIENT RECORD. *** Registration never collected a city, and this gateway marks it mandatory. See _comment_missing_client_fields.

billing_fields.name: country
billing_fields._comment: *** NOT ON THE CLIENT RECORD. *** The captured select offers exactly one option, AE (United Arab Emirates) — the gateway is scoped to the applying country, so this is effectively fixed per route. See _comment_missing_client_fields.

billing_fields.name: postcode
billing_fields._comment: *** NOT ON THE CLIENT RECORD. *** Mandatory here, and its container is the data-dependent-field of the country select, so it may appear or vanish when country changes. See _comment_missing_client_fields.

_comment_missing_client_fields: *** THREE MANDATORY GATEWAY FIELDS HAVE NO SOURCE: city, country_code, postcode. *** The client record holds first_name, last_name, email, phone_number, address_line_1 and address_line_2 — and nothing else this page needs. A run would fill six of nine fields and stop on the seventh, with the booking already made and unpaid. These must be added to registration (or defaulted per route) BEFORE this config is enabled. Discovered offline from a captured DOM rather than on a live payment, which is the entire point of capturing first.
_comment_submit: THE IRREVERSIBLE CLICK. name='commit', value='Pay', class='right complete pay_button' — NOT name='submit', which was the earlier guess and matches nothing. gateway.submit_payment fsyncs a journal row BEFORE this is clicked, and everything after it is read-only. Note the sibling: <input class='left cancelbutton' type='button' value='Cancel'> — addressing the submit by type alone would be ambiguous, so the name is part of the selector.
_comment_challenge: 3-D SECURE, AS OBSERVED LIVE ON 2026-10-14 (run 6acfa73ffbfcd5) — this is no longer a hypothesis. The bot NEVER completes the challenge: before the click it refuses outright, after the click it waits for a human and then reads the outcome (gateway._await_challenge). Markers are matched against the page URL AND EVERY IFRAME URL, which is what makes it work here.
_comment_challenge_observed: WHAT THE LIVE RUN SHOWED. 26 seconds after the Pay click the SAME TAB navigated to https://secureacceptance.cybersource.com/payer_authentication/hybrid?ccaAction=load — note the host: THE CHALLENGE LIVES ON THE GATEWAY'S OWN DOMAIN, not the bank's. The parent page carries two iframes: <iframe id='Cardinal-CCA-IFrame' height='600' width='500' title='Bank Authentication'> which holds the bank, and <iframe id='Cardinal-collector' height='0' width='0' style='display:none'> which is ThreatMetrix device fingerprinting and must NOT be mistaken for the challenge. Three child frames were live at that moment: https://geo.cardinalcommerce.com/DeviceFingerprintWeb/V2/Browser/Render?...origin=Songbird, the matching .../Notification, and the bank itself at https://acs.mashreq.com/BrowserChallenge/.
_comment_challenge_which_marker_fires: 'payer_auth' IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS, and it is the one to protect. It matches 'payer_authentication' in the PARENT url, which is served by CyberSource and is therefore THE SAME FOR EVERY ISSUER. The others are luck or issuer-specific: 'cca' matched only because the query string happened to read ccaAction=load, and 'acs'/'cardinalcommerce' matched the CHILD frames — but the ACS hostname belongs to the cardholder's bank (acs.mashreq.com here, something else for the next card), so nothing may depend on it. Do not remove 'payer_auth' thinking the others cover it.
_comment_challenge_is_not_always_an_otp: *** THE METHOD IS THE ISSUER'S CHOICE, NOT THE GATEWAY'S. *** Mashreq served an OUT-OF-BAND challenge on 2026-10-14: the captured frame holds <form id='oobForm' action='https://acs.mashreq.com/BrowserChallenge/Submit'> with NO code field at all — only hidden fields (ReferenceId, usrcul, instid, instcode, Screen, __RequestVerificationToken) and <button type='submit' name='oobContinue' value='true'>. The cardholder approves in the bank's app and presses Continue. Other issuers (WIO, for one) send a typed OTP instead, which is a text input and a submit in the same iframe. The waiting code is deliberately blind to the difference — it watches for the handback, never for a field — so both work without a config change, and the operator message names the screen rather than the method.
_comment_challenge_markers_must_not_matc: *** EVERY MARKER IS CHECKED AGAINST THE GATEWAY'S OWN URL AND MUST NOT MATCH IT. *** 'secureacceptance' is the trap: a marker that is a substring of it would make the CHECKOUT page itself look like a challenge, and submit_payment would then refuse the payment before the card was ever submitted — a run that spends a slot and never pays. Verified in tests/test_payment_gateway.py, not by eye.
_comment_otp_timeout: How long a HUMAN gets at the bank's challenge screen before the run gives up and reports the outcome as unknown. Ten minutes: a texted code usually expires in 3-5, so this leaves room for one resend, and an app approval needs the cardholder to find their phone and unlock it. Giving up does NOT cancel the payment — it is already submitted — it only ends the wait, which is why the number is generous rather than tight. For reference, the live run of 2026-10-14 took 59 seconds from challenge to handback.
_comment_return_url: THE OUTCOME IS IN THE RETURN URL, confirmed twice now. 2026-10-14: https://visa.vfsglobal.com/are/en/nor/confirmation?PaymentStatus=False&RequestRefNo=1049702718&TransactionId=7919938873246265404140&token= — reached directly from the challenge, with the page reading 'Sorry, your appointment may not have been completed successfully... If funds have been deducted from your account, log in after 30 minutes and check if your appointment is confirmed.' That run was a DELIBERATE DENIAL at the bank prompt, which is why PaymentStatus is False; it confirms the decline path end to end, not a fault.
